text_en: A good name is better than precious ointment, and the day of death, than the day of birth.
text_cn: 良好的声誉胜于名贵的香液；死日胜于生日。

text_en: It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting; for this is the end of everyone, and the living will lay it to heart.
text_cn: 往居丧的家去，胜于往宴会的家去，因为丧事是人人的结局，活人应将此事放在心上。

text_en: Sorrow is better than laughter, for by sadness of countenance the heart is made glad.
text_cn: 悲哀胜于欢笑，因为愁容能使心灵舒畅。

text_en: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
text_cn: 智者的心是在居丧的家中，愚人的心是在欢笑的家中。

text_en: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise than to hear the song of fools.
text_cn: 听智者斥责，胜过听愚人歌唱。

text_en: For like the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of fools; this also is vanity.
text_cn: 愚人的欢笑，就像釜底荆棘的爆炸声，但这也是空虚。

text_en: Surely oppression makes the wise foolish, and a bribe corrupts the heart.
text_cn: 实在，压榨使智者昏愚，贿赂能败坏人心。

text_en: Better is the end of a thing than its beginning; the patient in spirit are better than the proud in spirit.
text_cn: 事情的结局胜过事情的开端；居心宽容，胜过存心傲慢。

text_en: Do not be quick to anger, for anger lodges in the bosom of fools.
text_cn: 你心里不要轻易动怒，因为愤怒只停留在愚人胸中。

text_en: Do not say, “Why were the former days better than these? ” For it is not from wisdom that you ask this.
text_cn: 你不要问：“为什么昔日胜于今日？”因为这样的诘问，不是出于智慧。

text_en: Wisdom is as good as an inheritance, an advantage to those who see the sun.
text_cn: 智慧与家产都好，对看见天日的人都有益，

text_en: For the protection of wisdom is like the protection of money, and the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom gives life to the one who possesses it.
text_cn: 因为受智慧的荫庇与受金钱的荫庇无异；但认识智慧的好处，是在于智慧赋与有智慧者生命。

text_en: Consider the work of God; who can make straight what he has made crooked?
text_cn: 你应观察天主的作为：他所弯曲的，谁能使之正直？

text_en: In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider; God has made the one as well as the other, so that mortals may not find out anything that will come after them.
text_cn: 幸福之日，你应欢乐，不幸之日，你应思虑：幸与不幸，都是天主所为；其目的是为叫人不能察觉自己将来的事。

text_en: In my vain life I have seen everything; there are righteous people who perish in their righteousness, and there are wicked people who prolong their life in their evildoing.
text_cn: 在我虚度的岁月内，我见了许多事：义人在正义中夭亡，恶人在邪恶中反而长寿。

text_en: Do not be too righteous, and do not act too wise; why should you destroy yourself?
text_cn: 不要过于正义，也不要自作聪明，免得自趋灭亡。

text_en: Do not be too wicked, and do not be a fool; why should you die before your time?
text_cn: 不要作恶无度，也不要糊涂太甚，免得你死非其时。

text_en: It is good that you should take hold of the one, without letting go of the other; for the one who fears God shall succeed with both.
text_cn: 你的手最好把持这个，也不放弃那个，因为敬畏天主的人，二者兼顾并重。

text_en: Wisdom gives strength to the wise more than ten rulers that are in a city.
text_cn: 智慧使智者的权势，胜过本城十个有权势的人。

text_en: Surely there is no one on earth so righteous as to do good without ever sinning.
text_cn: 世上没有一个只行善，而不犯罪的义人。

text_en: Do not give heed to everything that people say, or you may hear your servant cursing you;
text_cn: 你不要倾心去听人说的一切闲话，免得你听到你的仆人诅咒你；

text_en: your heart knows that many times you have yourself cursed others.
text_cn: 因为你心里知道，你许多次也诅咒过别人。

text_en: All this I have tested by wisdom; I said, “I will be wise, ” but it was far from me.
text_cn: 这一切我都用智慧追究过；我宣称我将成个智者，然而智慧仍离我很远。

text_en: That which is, is far off, and deep, very deep; who can find it out?
text_cn: 所有的事，既深远，又玄奥，谁能穷究？

text_en: I turned my mind to know and to search out and to seek wisdom and the sum of things, and to know that wickedness is folly and that foolishness is madness.
text_cn: 我又专心致力于认识、考察事物，寻求智慧和事理，得知邪恶就是昏愚，昏愚就是狂妄。

text_en: I found more bitter than death the woman who is a trap, whose heart is snares and nets, whose hands are fetters; one who pleases God escapes her, but the sinner is taken by her.
text_cn: 我发觉女人比死亡还苦，她一身是罗网：她的心是陷阱，她的手是锁链；凡博天主欢心的，必逃避她；但罪人却被她缠住。

text_en: See, this is what I found, says the Teacher, adding one thing to another to find the sum,
text_cn: 训道者说：看，这是我所发现的，一一加以比较，好探知事物的原理，

text_en: which my mind has sought repeatedly, but I have not found. One man among a thousand I found, but a woman among all these I have not found.
text_cn: 对此我的心还在追求，但尚未找到：在一千男人中，我发现了一个；在所有的女人中，却没有发现一个。

text_en: See, this alone I found, that God made human beings straightforward, but they have devised many schemes.
text_cn: 我发现的只有这一件事：天主造人原很正直，但人却发明了许多诡计。
